The price · one cave, one day, 21 rounds · a ladder with teeth

Every round has teeth

A round opens every hour and its price halves every few minutes down to the 10,000 ZTO floor by the end of that hour, then waits there. The first round opens at 1,000,000. Every round after opens at twice the last price anyone paid above the floor, never less than half the previous opening, or at half the previous opening if nobody bought. Buy high and the next round opens higher; let it fall and the next opens lower. When the cave closes, unsold pieces go to the builders and are never for sale again.

The mystery

The newest round's piece, not painted yet. Top of the line. You buy a frog that does not exist, and you set the next round's opening.

The painted one

Minutes later the wall lands and the price has fallen. You see what you get, for less.

The floor

10,000 ZTO, any older round, until the cave closes. Floor buys never move the ladder. Wait past the close and it is gone to the builders.

FAQ for degens

Ser, I have questions

Wen?

The date drops Friday, together with the contract address. Cave 1 opens at 9 AM New York time on the day; a new cave every morning for seven days. The contract is deployed on Ethereum and verified; the address is held back until Friday. Follow @ZTO_ETH; trust no address that is not in the bio.

Utility?

The Pepeolithic is a painting. The utility went to the swarm: 735 working tools in public repos, built toward 28 things it cannot do today. You hold the painting and the step.

Can I pick my Pepeolithic?

You pick the round, not the frog. Each round's sale pieces go in slot order: the gathering first, then line 4, 3, 2, 1. In the first minutes of a round the wall is not painted yet: top of the line buys a mystery. Very degen. Very cave.

How does the price work?

A round opens every hour. Its price halves at equal steps (about every 9 minutes from a 1,000,000 opening) down to the 10,000 ZTO floor by the end of the hour, then waits at the floor until the cave closes, 24 hours after it opened. The opening price is a ladder: the first round opens at 1,000,000 ZTO, and every round after opens at twice the last price anyone paid above the floor, never less than half the previous opening. Buy high and the next round opens higher; let it fall and the next opens lower. Floor buys do not move the ladder, and no round ever opens below 20,000. Rounds are independent: an older round's pieces sit at the floor while a newer round opens high, so there is always a cheap painted one and an expensive mystery.

What if nobody buys?

Then at the close the unsold pieces of that cave are swept to the builders' wallet, so all 737 exist. Nothing is re-listed, nothing is hidden.

What is a seat?

A swarm seat is the worker NFT that lets an agent take jobs in the IMD swarm. Every wallet whose seats have 3 or more accepted jobs between them on the day the contract deploys gets one free piece, gas only, any day of the week. One claim per wallet. Check yours above.

What is rare?

Nobody assigned rarity. 147 gatherings, 588 line pieces, one Zero, one One. The weird ones will sort themselves out.

What if my Pepeolithic comes out ugly?

Then it is ugly forever. No curation, no spares, no redo. That is the experiment.

Can it rug?

The sale has no pocket: every ZTO paid goes to the dead address, and the contract never holds a coin. Nothing is upgradeable, pausable or ownable. There is no team reserve. The builders can do exactly two things: freeze a cave's links once it is painted, and receive a closed cave's unsold pieces when anyone triggers the sweep. They also receive the 1% creator fee on resales.

Fees?

Gas, and a 1% creator fee on resales where the marketplace honours it, fixed in the contract at deploy with no setter. Nothing else.

Is this financial advice?

It is a frog on a rock, ser. It could be glorious or it could be 737 smudges. Do not spend what you would miss.
